blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en:
Long-context large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong capabilities across a wide range of tasks, but the growing KV cache
introduces substantial memory and inference overhead. Existing one-shot KV cache compression methods typically commit to irreversible eviction immediately after prefill, before any signal from actual generation becomes available. Our quantitative analysis shows that early queries from the actual generation stage provide attention signals that are more consistent with subsequent decode attention, with the largest single-step gain occurring at the prefill–decode boundary. Based on this observation, we propose DeferKV, which moves the eviction decision from the end of prefill to the first real decoding step and temporally combines prompt-side and decode-side observations, thereby better aligning KV importance estimation with subsequent generation requirements. DeferKV requires no additional
training, draft model, or future-query prediction module, making it simple and easy to deploy.
Experiments on LongBench, RULER, and Needle-in-a-Haystack demonstrate
that DeferKV consistently improves model performance under KV cache
compression while maintaining low inference latency.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Large language models (LLMs) with long-context capabilities OpenAI (2023) ; Team (2025) have demonstrated strong performance in document question answering Dasigi et al. (2021) , multi-document
summarization Fabbri et al. (2019) , code understanding Bai et al. (2024) , retrieval-augmented generation Lewis et al. (2020) , and
complex reasoning Yao et al. (2023) . However, long-context inference also introduces
substantial system overhead. In particular, the KV cache has become a
major bottleneck affecting memory consumption and inference throughput Li et al. (2025) ; Shi et al. (2024) ; Yuan et al. (2024) .
For autoregressive Transformer decoders Vaswani et al. (2017) , the key and value
representations of historical tokens must be cached at every layer to
avoid redundant computation during generation. As the context length
increases, the memory consumption of the KV cache grows linearly with
the sequence length, making long-context inference more challenging on
memory-constrained devices and in high-concurrency serving scenarios.
Therefore, compressing the KV cache while preserving generation quality
has become an important research problem in efficient LLM inference.

However, these methods Li et al. (2024) ; Liu et al. (2025) typically rely on a key assumption: the queries
within the observation window at the end of the prompt are sufficient
to reflect the actual attention requirements of subsequent decoding.
This assumption does not always hold in long-text generation tasks. As shown in Figure 1 , more historical KV tokens lie closer to the diagonal when using the first real decode query. Its attention scores are therefore more consistent with subsequent decode attention than those aggregated from the final 32 prefill queries. This suggests that prompt-end attention alone may not fully capture the access patterns observed during subsequent generation. Consequently, estimating KV importance solely from prompt-side queries may lead to suboptimal token selection for later decoding.

Based on these observations, we propose a more direct and lightweight
approach. Unlike existing methods that rely solely on prompt-side information, our strategy postpones irreversible KV eviction until the first real decode-side signal becomes available and incorporates a small amount of attention feedback from actual generation. This explicitly aligns the importance estimation of historical tokens with
the requirements of subsequent decoding. We further consider how to
effectively integrate observations from the input and generation stages.
To this end, we introduce a simple yet effective temporal weighting
strategy to improve the reliability and accuracy of importance
estimation.

blocks.en: Our main contributions are summarized as follows:
blocks.zh: 我们的主要贡献概述如下:

blocks.en:

We propose a compression approach that postpones irreversible KV eviction until the earliest real decode-side feedback becomes available, thereby better aligning KV selection with subsequent decoding. • Our method is simple, direct, and lightweight. It does not require additional training, a draft model, an auxiliary network, or a future-query prediction module. state-of-the-art baselines under constrained KV cache budgets, achieving
relative performance gains of up to 3.58% on LongBench and 8.03% on
RULER.

blocks.en: 2.1 KV Cache Compression and Token Eviction
blocks.zh: 2.1 KV 缓存压缩和调试

blocks.en: To reduce the memory consumption of the KV cache, existing studies Zhang et al. (2023) ; Liu et al. (2023) have explored compression by reducing the number of cached tokens. These methods typically retain important Key-Value pairs according to the potential contribution of historical tokens to subsequent generation, while evicting KV entries with lower importance, thereby controlling the cache size during decoding. Prompt-only compression methods usually perform a one-time selection of prompt KV tokens after the prefill stage and before decoding begins Li et al. (2025) . They are generally simple to implement and introduce limited scheduling overhead.

blocks.en:
Prompt-side attention does not fully reflect the KV access requirements
of subsequent decoding, while the first real decode query provides a
more reliable signal and queries closer to decoding are generally more
informative. Based on these observations, DeferKV postpones KV cache
compression until after the first standard decoding step.

blocks.en:
As illustrated in Figure 3 , DeferKV obtains the first
real decode query from the target model and combines it with
recent prompt queries to form a decode-aware observation window. Their
attention scores are aggregated using temporal weighting, assigning

scores are used to estimate prompt-token importance and construct the
compressed KV cache for subsequent generation. In this
way, DeferKV better aligns KV selection with actual decoding requirements
without predicting future queries, introducing auxiliary models, or
altering the standard generation trajectory.

blocks.en: 6 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 6 结论

blocks.en: In this paper, we revisit a basic design choice in one-shot KV cache compression: when to commit to irreversible eviction. DeferKV moves this decision to the first decoding step, where real generation-side feedback becomes available, and uses temporal weighting to integrate the first real decode query with recent prompt queries. Extensive evaluations on LongBench, Needle-in-a-Haystack, and RULER show that DeferKV improves long-context performance with low inference latency. It requires no additional training, draft model, or auxiliary prediction module, providing a lightweight approach to efficient long-context inference.
blocks.zh: 在本文中,我们重新审视一发KV缓存压缩的基本设计选择:何时承诺不可逆转地驱逐. DeferKV将这个决定移动到第一个解码步骤,那里可以得到真正的生成侧反馈,并使用时间加权将第一个真正的解码查询与最近的即时查询整合. 对Long Bench、Needle-in-a-Haystack和RULAR的广泛评价表明,DeferKV以较低的推论延迟性改进了长文的性能。 它不需要额外的培训、模型草案或辅助预测模块,为高效的长文推论提供轻量级方法。

blocks.en: Limitations
blocks.zh: 限制

blocks.en: DeferKV postpones one-shot KV eviction until the earliest real decode query becomes available, which requires retaining the full prompt KV cache through the first decoding step. This design therefore shifts the memory reduction to subsequent decoding. Our experiments focus on models with standard token-wise KV caches under softmax attention. Extending DeferKV to architectures with different cache organizations, such as MLA or hybrid linear-attention models, may require architecture-specific adaptation.
blocks.zh: DeferKV推迟一发KV驱出,直到最早的真解码查询可用,这需要通过第一个解码步骤保留全部的快取KV缓存. 因此,这种设计将内存的还原转换为后续的解码. 我们的实验集中在 具有标准符号的 KV 缓存的模型 在软马克斯的注意力。 将DeferKV扩展至具有不同缓存组织的架构,如MLA或混合线性留念模型,可能需要对架构进行特异性改造.
